events.title: US equities close lower as Nvidia drop outweighs energy gains
events.summary: Traders working on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange on Nov 10, in New York City. US stocks closed lower as Nvidia fell after Jensen Huang’s exit, while energy shares rose on higher crude prices and Trump’s Iran comments. AI and chip stocks stayed volatile. Investors worried about tighter regulation, Nvidia leadership, and financing scrutiny, while some rivals and the energy sector gained. Markets now await the Producer Price Index. Traders expect a December Fed rate hike, with officials split on how aggressive policy should be. NEW YORK - US stocks closed lower on Nov 12, as a drop in Nvidia shares after CEO Jensen Huang’s exit outweighed gains in energy shares. The chip company’s shares fell but were well off the day’s lowest level after earlier dropping nearly 12%. Retail investors bought Nvidia shares worth about US$111 million (S$142 million) in the first half hour of trading, the biggest opening bid on record for the stock, according to data from Vanda Analytics. The S&P 500 energy index rose for a fourth straight session as the best-performing of the 11 major S&P sectors. Crude prices climbed after President Donald Trump wrote on social media that the US did not need a deal with Iran. Global AI-linked stocks fell and AI cloud firm Nebius tumbled after reporting its quarterly earnings and outlook. But Nvidia competitors such as Broadcom, Advanced Micro Devices, Alphabet and Amazon moved higher and were among the biggest boosts to the S&P 500. Equities have been volatile in recent days. Sweeping Democratic victories in the US midterm elections have sparked investor concern about more AI regulation. Worries about Nvidia’s leadership have also pressured one of the foundations of the current bull market. Nvidia tabbed chief financial officer Colette Kress as interim CEO. “Right now, the market is selling AI stocks and tech stocks and buying safe stuff, just like it did in the first halo trade in January and February of this year, but it will flip back,” said Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager at Argent Capital Management in St Louis. “That’s the tug of war the market is doing right now. It’s concerns about deceleration versus just pointing out that the absolute valuation and growth rates are still pretty compelling.” According to preliminary data, the S&P 500 lost 25.99 points, or 0.34%, to end at 7,593.39 points, while the Nasdaq Composite lost 102.44 points, or 0.40%, to 25,363.75. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 190.29 points, or 0.36%, to 52,296.20. Even with Huang’s departure, some investors expect questions to persist about the future of AI companies with strong ties to Nvidia. The company has backed several firms, including its own customers, through financing arrangements that face greater scrutiny after Huang’s departure. “Nvidia is the circular-funder-in-chief; they’re the biggest by far at this point, and I assume that activity will moderate,” said Ellerbroek. The Philadelphia Semiconductor index declined after surging 17.2% over the prior four sessions. Along with Nebius, peer CoreWeave dropped. Shares of data centre-related firms IREN and Applied Digital also slumped. Investors are awaiting the release of the Producer Price Index on Nov 13, which will follow a hotter-than-expected consumer price reading earlier this week. Markets are completely pricing in a December rate hike of at least 25 basis points by the Federal Reserve, with a 15% chance of a 50-basis-point increase, according to CME FedWatch. Comments from multiple Fed officials earlier this week suggested the US central bank was open to a more aggressive path of rate hikes as price pressures worsen. Cleveland Fed president Beth Hammack said on Nov 12 she does not believe the central bank needs to shift to more aggressive rate hikes to combat inflation, while San Francisco Federal Reserve president Mary Daly said she thinks the central bank will likely need to raise interest rates further to deal with elevated inflation, but did not suggest any urgency. events.title: Jensen Huang, an architect of the AI boom, resigns as Nvidia CEO
events.summary: Jensen Huang resigned as CEO of Nvidia after he reportedly had two affairs, including one with a purported Chinese spy. Why it matters: It's impossible to overstate how critical Huang is to Nvidia, to the AI buildout, to the stock market and economy. His departure could, per Wall Street sources, be the catalyst that endangers a ballooning AI bubble. It's also unlikely to ease congressional scrutiny of the company or Huang himself. Driving the news: Nvidia's board named longtime CFO Colette Kress interim CEO, while launching a search for a permanent replacement. Kress, who joined Nvidia in 2013, will continue serving as CFO while overseeing the company. Harvey C. Jones was appointed Nvidia's first-ever board chair. The board said it expects Nvidia's operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption. What they're saying: " I believe deeply in this company and in its future. More than anything, I believe in each of you, in our customers and partners and in the vital role we play every day in the global economy," Kress said in a note to staff after the news came out. "We play a vital role in building the technology that is powering the AI revolution, and we have important work ahead of us. So let's move forward together, with the same determination and commitment that have always defined this company," she added. Zoom out: Huang's resignation follows revelations about two extramarital relationships. The New York Times reported Wednesday that Huang had a relationship with Kimberly Powell, a senior Nvidia executive who reports to him. Nvidia's board had previously launched an independent investigation into Huang's relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman identified by U.S. intelligence as a Chinese intelligence asset. Nvidia did not provide a reason for Huang's resignation in Thursday's announcement, which comes after reports that the board had an emergency meeting over whether to oust the CEO. By the numbers: Nvidia shares fell as much as 13% after news of Huang's resignation before rebounding somewhat. One of Wall Street's most prominent voices on tech, analyst Dan Ives, said Nvidia was worth 25% less without Huang. 🚨 Stunning stat: At these levels, Nvidia will have lost about $1.4 trillion in market capitalization in two weeks, since the initial Times report about linking Jensen Huang and Alice Huang. The big picture: This will likely go down as one of the biggest executive scandals in history. Nvidia is also one of the largest holdings in major index funds because of its size, meaning this move has massive implications for every American with a retirement account. The intrigue: Huang's resignation doesn't look like it'll ease congressional pressure over his behavior either. "NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang's decision to resign does not absolve him, other executives, or the company as a whole of responsibility for putting our national security at risk or for any potential violations of our laws," Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) said in a statement. The bottom line: The fallout is just starting. This is breaking news.

events.title: United Airlines wants you to check in, not your chatbot
events.summary: United Airlines has become the latest company to slap restrictions on unauthorized third-party AI agents, warning that the bots could make unintended purchases, expose customer data, or bypass checks requiring human acknowledgment. The airline announced restrictions covering both its own digital platforms and indirect access through travel agencies and aggregators, with changes to its booking, ticketing, and distribution policies. United says automated actions could violate aviation regulations, citing the requirement for a human acknowledgment during check-in that bags contain no banned substances. A bot cheerfully ticking the box isn't quite the passenger confirmation it has in mind. And then there is the worry that "sharing account credentials with personal, third-party, AI assistants can expose sensitive information, and actions taken by these tools may result in unintended purchases, account changes, or use of MileagePlus miles." United would also rather customers use its own app than turn third-party assistants loose on its systems. AI agents are pitched as a way to outsource life's minutiae, and it's difficult to navigate the web without tripping over a breathless influencer explaining why you need one, or dozens, or hundreds of virtual personal assistants. The thing is that operating these assistants requires care and thought. Earlier this year, British mathematician Professor Hannah Fry conducted a cautionary experiment in which she gave an AI agent a bank card, and a bit too much agency, to see what it would do. Passwords were coughed up, and some ill-considered purchases were made. Still, as Fry said of the agent, dubbed Cassandra, "don't let her incompetence fool you, because these things are getting better fast." Last month, reports emerged of major US banks blocking third-party AI agents from operating inside accounts and taking actions on behalf of the customer. This month, several UK banks were reported to have followed suit. United stated: "Corporate leaders in the banking and retail industries have taken similar actions regarding AI agents and we encourage others to consider measures that preserve the data and security of their customers and strengthen safety." The Register asked United Airlines how it planned to implement the blocking. There are a few options, including physical biometric confirmation for actions or checking for signs of automated browser driving. Amazon has also moved against unauthorized AI agents, blocking Meta's Muse (the "AI that gets it done," according to Meta's marketing) in September . The airline has yet to respond. ®

events.title: Who is Nvidia's interim CEO Colette Kress - and who could take over permanently?
events.summary: Arm's boss Rene Haas (L), Nvidia's Colette Kress (C) and Chris Malachowsky (R) have been named as possible successors Nvidia is now facing a scenario few would have considered until very recently - a future without Jensen Huang. The influential co-founder of the AI chip-making giant resigned on Thursday over reports of extramarital affairs, one of which was with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. Chief financial officer Colette Kress is in charge, for now, as the tech giant faces one of its biggest challenges - finding the right person to permanently lead the business that Huang helped create more than three decades ago and turned into one of the world's most valuable companies. We take a look at which candidates have emerged as potential successors. Colette Kress is chief financial officer at Nvidia Colette Kress has been an industry veteran for more than 30 years, having previously held high positions at tech firms like Cisco and Microsoft. Kress, who also serves as Nvidia's executive vice-president, has seen the firm's transformation from making chips for video games in the early 1990s to becoming an AI semiconductor powerhouse. She has "fronted every earnings call" alongside Huang and is a "familiar and trusted voice for the market at a time when it badly needs one," said Josh Gilbert, an analyst at investment firm eToro. But doing the job permanently could be a different story, said Gilbert, as the firm, known for its edge in technology, could want an engineer in the chair. Chris Malachowsky is one of Nvidia's three co-founders Another option is Chris Malachowsky, who founded Nvidia alongside Huang and Curtis Priem, and is the only executive that shares the same level of seniority. Malachowsky has played a key part in developing the company's computing technology. Ian Buck, who oversees Nvidia's high-performance computing business, has also emerged as a potential candidate if the company is keen to put an engineer in the top job. Buck was among the early pioneers who helped popularise the use of graphic processors beyond gaming applications. "He could protect Nvidia's technological edge, but his ability to manage the wider commercial relationships and geopolitical challenges would face scrutiny," said Charu Chanana, investment strategist at investment bank Saxo. Today, Nvidia's leading processors are widely regarded as the gold standard for AI development. Huang's children also work at Nvidia in executive positions but are relatively young and inexperienced. Nvidia is likely to favour an internal appointment initially but could look externally for a more permanent replacement, said Jun Bei Liu, founder and lead portfolio manager at Ten Cap. Several names of tech entrepreneurs outside of Nvidia have been floated by experts. US President Donald Trump suggested Apple's former chief executive, Tim Cook, as a good replacement. "NOW THAT Nvidia CEO JENSEN HUANG, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one man to take his place - TIM COOK of Apple. A Legend replaces a Legend!" he wrote on Truth Social. Liu said Cook could be a possible choice as someone familiar with managing global supply chains, though she questioned whether he would be willing to leave the iPhone maker, where he is the chair. Apple's Tim Cook (R) with Jensen Huang (L) and his wife Lori Huang at the White House Liu and Chanana also suggested Rene Haas, chief executive of Arm Holdings, the UK chip designer. Nvidia's processors are made with the help of chipmakers around the world, including Taiwan's TSMC and South Korea's SK Hynix and Samsung. Rene Haas is the boss of Arm Holdings Haas is familiar with leading a publicly-listed company and would bring semiconductor experience, though Nvidia's business model is considerably different from Arm's, said Chanana. "The challenge is finding someone who can combine Jensen's technical understanding, strategic vision and relationships across the global technology industry," Liu said. Ten Cap's Liu had believed it was just a matter of time before Huang would step down as Nvidia's chief executive. "The issue is no longer simply about personal conduct," she said. "It is about corporate governance, national security concerns and maintaining confidence in the leadership of one of the world's most strategically important companies." Several major investment firms have downgraded their forecasts for the chip giant - a rare shift given investors' longstanding optimism about the company. An early indication came as markets opened in New York shortly after Huang's resignation was announced. Nvidia shares opened down more than 13%, wiping more than half a trillion dollars off the firm's share market value. Jensen Huang's departure leaves a void in the influential AI giant Stacy Rasgon, senior analyst in US semiconductors at Bernstein Research, wrote in a note to investors that "our gut tells us we probably haven't fully probed the depths of what might be found here".

events.title: Nvidia CEO’s ouster leaves AI world reeling
events.summary: The News Jensen Huang was ousted as Nvidia’s CEO Thursday, a stunning fall for one of the world’s most powerful figures. His downfall sparked fears of what his departure means for one of America’s chip champions and the unwind of the AI money machine he assembled. Nvidia’s CFO, Colette Kress, will serve as interim CEO while the board conducts a search for Huang’s replacement. Huang will also leave the board, which he chaired, and will be replaced by Harvey Jones, a board member since Nvidia’s founding in 1993 who ran chip design company Synopsys in the 1980s and 1990s. Semafor had earlier reported that Kress was in the lead to run the company on a temporary basis. The company said it will look at both internal and external permanent successors to Huang, whose departure leaves the giant chipmaker without a tested leader. Huang had nearly single-handedly turned Nvidia from a niche maker of graphics chips for video games into the centerpiece of the world’s AI boom, and the company has never had another leader. It has no succession plan and few apparent internal successors. One external candidate under consideration is Apple hardware chief Johny Srouji, who was among the executives considered for Intel CEO in 2019, Semafor reported Wednesday. Other names that have been floated are AMD’s Lisa Su, Huang’s first cousin once removed, as well as an offbeat suggestion by US President Trump on Thursday to tap former Apple CEO Tim Cook for the job. Huang’s ouster came four days after he admitted to an affair with a suspected Chinese spy and followed a New York Times report that he had another affair with a subordinate. He is now wrapped up in a series of investigations by the board, congressional leaders, and by the Department of Justice , Semafor reported on Thursday. The ongoing saga has also shaved hundreds of billions of dollars off of what was once the world’s most valuable company — one crucial to the US remaining at the forefront of AI development around the world. Shares fell as much as 7% Thursday, adding to Nvidia’s losses since the first reports of Huang’s relationship with the suspected Beijing spy, who ran a Singaporean company that was a major buyer of Nvidia’s advanced chips. Shares of neoclouds Nebius and CoreWeave, which rely on Nvidia to help AI startups rent space in their data centers, fell as much as 19% and 9%, respectively. Shares in Alphabet, whose TPU chips compete with Nvidia’s GPUs, rose slightly. Key-man risk Huang’s ouster raises questions around Nvidia’s ability to remain the de facto central bank of the AI boom — and the fate of billions of dollars of chip financing from a slew of Wall Street firms that are tangled up with the company. Nvidia has provided tens of billions of dollars in financing to its customers, invested more than $50 billion in AI startups, and guaranteed huge data-center leases for firms including OpenAI. Much of that spending rested on Huang’s singular credibility and power in the tech world, as well as his close ties to US President Donald Trump. His successor will likely have far less leeway from the chipmaker’s board, which is facing its own mountain of litigation, government investigations, and public scrutiny. Still, Huang will remain one of Nvidia’s largest shareholders, with a 3.6% stake in the company worth about $160 billion at today’s price. While he doesn’t have the same sort of control afforded to other tech founders through super-voting stock, such as Alphabet’s Larry Page and Sergey Brin, he’ll maintain a meaningful seat at the table. It’s unclear what his exit package looks like and whether the board will claw back any additional share-based compensation from previous years. Washington fallout Rep. Brian Mast, R-Fla., chair of the House Foreign Affairs Committee who’s been pushing for stricter export control laws, said Thursday that Huang agreed to come in for a closed-door briefing before lawmakers break again for Thanksgiving on Nov. 20. Other Congress members have sent letters asking Huang to come and testify in Washington. Meanwhile, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is under increasing pressure from members of Congress over how his office allowed Nvidia to sell its advanced chips to what reports allege to be a front for banned Chinese buyers. The Trump administration is made more vulnerable by Huang’s close relationship with Trump and its deference to the Nvidia CEO on chip policy matters. “This incident raises significant concerns about the federal government’s ability to effectively enforce our export controls and protect our national security,” Sens. Chris Coons, D-Del., and Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., wrote in a letter to Lutnick, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, and White House chief of staff Stephen Miller on Thursday, asking them to preserve documents related to Nvidia. Reports suggest government officials “were aware of concerns about Nvidia, its relationship with Megaspeed, and the suspected Chinese intelligence operation, yet did not move to block the continued flow of advanced AI chips,” the senators said. So far, Trump is standing by Lutnick. The president “maintains complete confidence in the secretary and his ability to carry out the position,” a White House official told Semafor. Winners and losers Huang’s exit could scramble the AI chip market, elevate rivals that have been relegated to operating in Nvidia’s shadow, and ensure more chips stay in the US rather than in China, which could explain hyperscalers’ share rises Thursday. While long chip design cycles mean it could take years for a competitor to eat into Nvidia’s lead, a few companies stand out as beneficiaries. AMD, whose stock is surging, competes most directly with Nvidia on data-center products. Broadcom and other custom silicon makers could gain as tech giants look to design more of their own chips, rather than relying on Nvidia’s. Google may also get more momentum on its TPUs, which it began selling directly to outside customers this year. And Qualcomm offers a competing line of chips for robots. China’s chipmakers are also poised to benefit: Any tightening of US chip export controls could push more resources toward building out China’s domestic chip sector, a long-term priority of Beijing’s. And China hawks in Washington are newly empowered to push for more restrictions on American chipmakers’ overseas dealings.

events.title: Nvidia without Huang is like Apple without Jobs: A cash spigot without real innovation
events.summary: Some Silicon Valley executives are quietly celebrating Jensen Huang’s ouster from Nvidia and the national furor over chip exports to China. The good news for American companies is that tech exports that were going to China are now expected to be redirected to US firms, one person told me. That could accelerate the growth of the big AI labs and other Silicon Valley companies, and hobble Chinese rivals. In the short term, they’re probably right. There’s strong evidence that export controls have successfully slowed China’s technological progress. The problem is that the US can’t win the technological race with China in the long term by slowing its rival down. The bigger and more difficult part of that victory is speeding up American innovation. And that’s where Huang’s ouster is a counter-force to the gains made on China policy. Huang is one of Silicon Valley’s great innovators. In the short term, his ouster won’t be terrible for Nvidia. Nvidia may actually become a more profitable company now, because any new CEO will optimize for profitability, as Apple did under Tim Cook. Innovators burn a lot of money thinking about the long term. And Nvidia will never be as innovative as it was under Huang. Huang was Nvidia’s one-man, long-term moat. That’s especially true now, in an era when AI allows pretty much any company to design a chip just like Nvidia’s, as OpenAI did in a matter of months. A less innovative Nvidia is not just a problem for Nvidia. It’s a problem for the entire technology ecosystem. Big, powerful incumbents tend to be barriers to innovation. Cook’s Apple built the iPhone and then sat on that invention by defending its turf — a great business strategy but one that let the entire mobile ecosystem stagnate. The key risk to the US tech industry isn’t that Chinese spies will steal its cutting-edge technology. It’s that Silicon Valley is at risk of seeing the magic formula that brought that technology into being in the first place weakened.

events.title: Microsoft Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 enter their 'permanently vulnerable' era
events.summary: Microsoft has warned customers still clinging to Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 to consider the software "permanently vulnerable" as November's security fixes arrive for Subscription Edition (SE) alone. The warning appears in the release documentation for November's Exchange Server SE security update. Looking for Exchange 2016 and 2019 information? Tough. Microsoft stated: "Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 are no longer tested for vulnerabilities and there are no updates released. If you are using those versions of Exchange, you should consider them permanently vulnerable [Microsoft's emphasis] and should upgrade your organization immediately." You have been warned. Support for Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 ended on October 14, 2025, but the company announced an Extended Security Updates (ESU) program in July 2025. The plan was that this program would end on April 14, 2026, by which time customers would surely have made the jump to a later or online version, right? The company said: "This period will not be extended past April 2026 (you do not need to ask)." And... of course it was. As April 2026 rolled around, and it became clear that some customers were still stubbornly sticking with the old versions, Microsoft did the equivalent of heaving an exasperated sigh and offered another six months of paid security updates. Those final weeks also brought a separate treat: a Windows Server update breaking Exchange Server . This time it was serious. Microsoft released the final Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 security updates on October 13. No more patches, no more vulnerability testing, and apparently no more reprieves. According to Microsoft's Security Update Guide , the November update fixed nine vulnerabilities in Exchange Server SE, including a critical remote code execution flaw, CVE-2026-118207. Microsoft isn't testing earlier versions of Exchange for the vulnerabilities. ®

events.title: Global AI stocks sink as Nvidia CEO’s exit deepens sector sell-off
events.summary: Jensen Huang’s exit plunges the US$4 trillion (S$5.14 trillion) company into uncertainty and threatens to disrupt an AI ecosystem. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned after a scandal, and CFO Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO while the company searches for a permanent leader. Global AI stocks fell as Nvidia shares slid 10.3% pre-market, with the firm losing about US$300 billion since its Nov 8 investigation and facing funding and regulatory worries. Rivals like AMD and Broadcom rose on hopes of market share gains, while other chip and neocloud stocks dropped and tech markets in Asia and Europe also weakened. Global AI-linked stocks tumbled on Nov 12 as Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned following a deepening scandal around his affairs, upending the chipmaker’s leadership and posing fresh risks to a sector already reeling with funding and regulatory concerns. Chief financial officer Colette Kress will take over as interim CEO as Nvidia looks for a permanent successor, the company said. As the centrepiece of the AI ecosystem, the chipmaker finances infrastructure built around its chips – a strategy that has drawn scrutiny over circular funding and now risks weighing on the sector as its crisis deepens. Nvidia’s shares fell 8.2% to a more than 16-month low in early trading and its market value was on track to close below US$4 trillion (S$5.14 trillion) for the first time since July 2025. “Nvidia has been called the ‘Bank of AI’. If they have to take a step back because of what’s going on, will that cut off funding to smaller companies that need it? That’s an open question,” said Joe Saluzzi, partner and co-head of equity trading at Themis Trading. Nvidia-backed neocloud firms CoreWeave dropped 9.1 % after surging more than 27% in the previous session when its earnings ignited a relief rally in AI stocks. Other neocloud stocks including IREN and Applied Digital were also trading lower. Nebius dropped 16.2 % after the company said its 2026 revenue would come in at the low end of its previous forecast. Nvidia has lost about US$550 billion in market value since the board announced an investigation on Nov 8 into Huang’s relationship with a businesswoman called Alice Huang , who is alleged to be a Chinese spy. “The interlocking deals that Nvidia has with so much of the industry raises the question of whether that created more stability or more fragility. We’re going to find out over the next few weeks as this whole situation unravels,” said Steve Sosnick, chief market analyst at Interactive Brokers. Nvidia short sellers have made US$9.6 billion in on-paper profits so far this week, according to data analytics firm ORTEX. AI sell-off continues after brief respite Chipmakers, widely viewed as one of the biggest beneficiaries of the AI boom, led the sell-off, with the Philadelphia chips index sliding 1.3%. Marvell Technology, which Huang called as the “next trillion-dollar company” in June, slumped 3.8%. AI hyperscaler Oracle, which is expanding its cloud AI chip deals with Nvidia, shed 2.6%. Memory chipmaker Micron Technology fell 2.5 % and data storage firms Sandisk and Western Digital eased 6 % and 3.7 %. Photonic product makers Lumentum and Coherent and AI server maker Dell eased between 3% and 5.1%. Construction and power-generation equipment maker Caterpillar and power producer Vistra slipped about 0.5% each. Other hyperscalers including Alphabet, Amazon.com and Microsoft were also up between 0.8% and 2.7%. AI stocks struggled and the Nasdaq entered a technical correction earlier in November after the Democrats swept the US midterm elections, including in states opposed to data centres, stoking fears tighter regulation could slow the AI build-out. Tech-heavy stock markets across the globe witnessed jitters. Japan and South Korea closed nearly 0.7% lower. Tech stocks in Europe were also down about 1%. Nvidia trades at about 12 times its 12-month forward earnings estimates, its lowest since November 2012, according to data compiled by LSEG. REUTERS

events.title: Poundland gets more time to secure a rescue deal as emergency talks continue
events.summary: Poundland has avoided immediate collapse after a deadline was extended to find a rescue deal. A deadline to secure a buyer for the retail chain was set to expire at midnight, but a court has given Poundland an extra 10 days to find a buyer. The discount chain, which has 11,000 employees, has been edging towards administration after being blocked by owners Gordon Brothers from accessing cash in its bank accounts. A committee of MPs questioned Gordon Brothers following accusations that the investment firm hoped to profit from selling off Poundland's 600 shops and stock piecemeal. Gordon Brothers - which bought the chain for just £1 last year - is accused of forcing that outcome by restricting Poundland's access to available cash needed to restock shops, and pay wages and rent, ahead of the crucial Christmas trading period. The investment firm, which specialises in buying and restructuring distressed companies, has denied the claims. However, pressure remains on Poundland's owners after a takeover bid was rejected. The decision prompted calls for answers from politicians, including Prime Minister Andy Burnham. About £50m had been frozen by Gordon Brothers, the BBC understands, meaning Poundland bosses were unable to restock shelves across its 600 shops. The BBC understands that Gordon Brothers agreed to release a further £11m today from Poundland's accounts, on top of £10m announced earlier, as the firm seeks to find a new buyer. Gordon Brothers said it was in talks with three parties for a sale of the whole business, and it had received "several offers from established high street retailers for significant parts of the business". Following the meeting between MPs on the business and trade committee and representatives of Gordon Brothers, chairman Liam Byrne told the BBC that he was "deeply concerned" and described the firm's behaviour as "much like a wolf on Wall Street, on the British High Street". "They refused to prioritise protecting jobs and stores over and above their own financial returns," he said. "It's clear that they've taken millions out of Poundland at a time when they themselves said the business was on a knife edge." Byrne said the committee's message to Gordon Brothers was to ensure Poundland had "access to the funds that it needs to trade at what should be one of the busiest periods in the year". He urged Gordon Brothers to "do what is right to save jobs and stores and do that now". "It's a good business, it's a much-loved business and, particularly in the middle of the cost of living crisis, communities up and down the country rely on access to the kind of stores that it operates," Byrne added. Views on Poundland performance differ Views on the chain's performance differ between those running operations and the owners. Poundland boss Williams told staff last week that like-for-like sales, which exclude new store openings, were up 11.4%. The sales period included Halloween, but Williams said this was £1.5m ahead of budget. He added that the business made a profit of £18.1m in the year to September, which was a "strong recovery" from the previous year when there were losses of £68m. However, Gordon Brothers has painted a different picture, saying the chain remains "challenged and vulnerable to any potential downturn in future trading". It has argued that the best way of securing jobs may be to split up the business and sell chunks of its 600 sites to other retailers. There has been interest from the likes of Poundstretcher, Tesco and B&M in picking up Poundland shops, which could mean continuing employment for workers at those sites. The main issue is whether a piecemeal sale would protect more jobs than a buyer willing to keep Poundland as a national chain. Are you affected by issues discussed in this story? events.title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia chief executive
events.summary: Nvidia's Jensen Huang has resigned as CEO of the company, following the revelation of his affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy and reports of a relationship with another woman who was a company employee. In a Form 8-K [PDF] filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), the GPU maker disclosed that it accepted the resignation of Huang, whom it identified as Jen-Hsun Huang, on November 11, effective immediately. He is being replaced by chief financial officer Colette Kress, who will serve as interim leader while the board conducts a search for a new CEO. Huang, who founded Nvidia in 1993 and served as president, CEO, and a member of the board of directors ever since, led the GPU maker to become one of the most valuable companies in the world, hitting a hit peak of over $5.5 trillion earlier this year. His position became untenable following an investigation by the company's board after he admitted to an affair, amid allegations he had a romantic relationship with a woman the US authorities suspected as a Chinese spy. Reports later surfaced this week of a second alleged affair with an employee of the company itself, reported by the New York Times as being with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of health care. A two-week downfall News of the scandal first broke barely a couple of weeks ago, on October 29, when claims surfaced that Huang had been the target of an espionage plot involving a Chinese businesswoman working for a Singapore-based company called Megaspeed which was a customer of Nvidia. According to the New York Times , US intelligence had reason to believe the woman, Alice Huang, was recruited to gather information about Nvidia and its operations for the Beijing government. Megaspeed also faces claims it was illicitly shipping Nvidia products to China, in violation of US export controls. Any relationship between Huang and a Chinese operative would be enormously concerning, as the US has been trying to keep advanced technology for AI out of the hands of the country, allegedly for security reasons, fearing it might be used for military purposes. For its part, Beijing rejects the spying allegations, saying they are part of a smear campaign against China. Shortly after Nvidia’s board announced it was investigating Huang, he sent an email to Nvidia staff apologizing and confessing to having an affair, though he did not explicitly name Alice Huang in his public apology. It seemed like the leather-jacketed leader might just hang on, since it was difficult to imagine anyone other than him leading the company after all this time. But Nvidia’s shares fell 4.3 percent on November 9 and a further 5.5 percent the following day, wiping around $430 billion off its market value, amid all the speculation. Then the claim emerged regarding a second affair, with an employee at Nvidia who reported to him, and many commentators took it as a sign the game was up. Huang resigned the same day the news broke. Indecision ahead Now the speculation starts over who will take over the reins at Nvidia, but Huang could prove a tough act to follow. He is said to have recognized early on the potential for taking the number-crunching capabilities of graphics processors and putting them to use at accelerating AI processing, and Nvidia’s position today as the leading AI hardware firm is thanks to that bet. “The sudden resignation of Jensen Huang is about more than succession at the world’s most important AI chipmaker, Nvidia’s leadership crisis is a stress test for the AI boom,” says Forrester VP and group research director Stephanie Balaouras. If Nvidia stabilizes quickly under new leadership, the AI infrastructure boom will have demonstrated resilience, she adds. But if its stock or financing relationships remain under sustained pressure, that would add evidence to the fragility of the AI bubble. “In the near term, the board did the sensible thing and reached for a steward. Colette Kress knows every number in that order book,” commented Mark Malek, CIO at financial services firm Siebert Financial. “It does NOT settle the stock. Interim means the real decision is still ahead, the investigations are still open, and next week’s earnings call just became the most important in the company’s history,” he added. ®

events.title: Meet Colette Kress, Nvidia’s New Interim CEO
events.summary: Nvidia’s CEO and cofounder Jensen Huang is officially out , and longtime chief financial officer Colette Kress is in. The chipmaker’s board of directors announced Thursday that Kress, who joined Nvidia in 2013, has been named interim CEO following Huang’s resignation amid a scandal over his extramarital affair with a Chinese businesswoman believed by US officials to be an asset of China’s Ministry of State Security. Harvey Jones, the newly appointed chair of Nvidia’s board, said in a statement that Kress “has helped lead Nvidia through a period of extraordinary growth and has a deep understanding of our business, customers, operations and financial position.” He added that Kress will be supported by an “experienced leadership team” and that the board has “full confidence” in her. Kress was among the most obvious candidates to fill the void after Huang’s departure, according to multiple tech executives and industry analysts who follow Nvidia closely, given her long tenure at the company, credibility on Wall Street and across the tech industry, and, perhaps most importantly, her deep familiarity with Nvidia’s business and finances. “She’s extremely strong-willed, professional, and whip-smart. She doesn’t tolerate nonsense. She can be friendly and gracious too,” says a former Nvidia executive who spoke on the condition of anonymity. “She obviously has a keen sense for how Jensen thinks.” “Colette is the logical choice,” says Patrick Moorhead, founder and chief analyst at Moor Insights & Strategies, who has tracked the chip industry for decades. “She has credibility with investors because she answers hard questions directly.” Moorhead says Kress has operated as much more than a “numbers” CFO. “In my conversations with her, she goes deep on the product road map, from rack-scale systems to networking and software,” he says. Nvidia’s board said on Sunday it was launching an independent investigation into Huang’s activities following a report by The New York Times that he had an affair with a woman named Alice Huang, who US officials suspected of being a Chinese intelligence asset. WIRED reported on Monday that Huang quietly hired a crisis communications firm sometime last year to handle matters related to his personal life. By October of 2025, the firm was being looped in on all press inquiries involving Huang at Nvidia, around the same time The New York Times reported that US authorities were investigating whether a company linked to Alice Huang had helped Chinese firms evade US chip export controls through its subsidiaries. While Huang has long been the public face of Nvidia, Kress has been responsible for managing the chipmaker’s relationship with Wall Street. On earnings calls, she often details Nvidia’s financial performance, customer demand, supply constraints, and other key metrics. “One of the things we don’t focus on is the stock price. We focus on our investors and how we would like to innovate,” Kress told the Israeli business newspaper Globes in 2023. Before joining Nvidia, Kress spent more than two decades in finance roles at Microsoft, Cisco, and Texas Instruments. Huang personally recruited her in 2013, when Nvidia was still best known for its gaming graphics cards, according to Globes. Huang laid out his vision for the company’s future on a whiteboard, explaining how Nvidia could become a major supplier of computing infrastructure for artificial intelligence. Other potential successors to Huang included Ian Buck, an Nvidia veteran of more than 20 years who created the company’s software platform CUDA and now oversees its high-performance computing business, and Jeff Fisher, who joined Nvidia in 1994 as the head of software sales and later became senior vice president of its GeForce unit, where he led Nvidia’s strategy for bringing GPUs to market. However, Nvidia’s unusual corporate structure has long meant that dozens of executives reported directly to Huang. The company lacks a traditional chief operating officer. Even executive vice presidents aren’t necessarily given direct control over budgets, sources have told WIRED. As a result, few people within the organization have the same level of understanding of the company’s financials as Kress. The former Nvidia executive who spoke to WIRED on the condition of anonymity said that while Kress is incredibly sharp and “can step into the [CEO] role immediately without needing any guidance,” she doesn’t have the same engineering and technical expertise that Huang brought to the role. She has also shied away from being “at the center of public attention,” the person said. Given the intense scrutiny surrounding Huang lately, that leadership style might be a welcome temporary change for Nvidia. events.title: The end of the 'Nvidia put' that powers the AI ecosystem
events.summary: Liz’s view Jensen Huang is out, and with him goes the “Nvidia put” that has underpinned the entire AI ecosystem. Huang, who resigned from his post Thursday, was the AI world’s central bank chairman and human security blanket, always there with a checkbook to backstop, acquire, hire, invest in, or otherwise underwrite the least underwritable corners of AI. That “put” — finance speak for a guaranteed buyer on the other side of a trade — has kept the AI financing and fundraising markets lubricated, even as it invited criticism of their circularity. It’s also helped prop up the stock market and padded 401(k)s for the last couple of years. Nvidia guarantees more than $100 billion of data-center leases , owns $51 billion worth of stock in privately held companies, and another $63 billion in listed ones. Its balance sheet was a sponge that absorbed the market’s growing AI fears and put a floor under deal prices. Whoever replaces him will face much higher stakes, akin to Tim Cook after Steve Jobs at Apple. They’ll also be on a tighter leash from a board of directors I suspect will get a much-needed refresh by the time this saga is over. (It’s hard to imagine the former president of Taco Bell or the former chief marketing officer of the NFL probing Huang too deeply on off-balance-sheet lease guarantees for next-generation data centers.) Not only will that change the fabric of one of the world’s most valuable companies, but it will also push up the price of AI debt and equity — making the AI buildout more expensive for everyone — by taking a huge buyer off the table. Notable Unlike with the 2008 financial crisis, “this time we can see it on a blue-sky day: Nvidia is officially too big to fail, ” I wrote in October. “What would be revealed by a stress test of Nvidia that contemplated a rise in the cost of AI-linked debt, a decline in venture-backed startup values, and a slowdown in data-center construction?” What happens under new leadership will determine the future of the company.

events.title: Jensen Huang's ouster triggers an AI earthquake
events.summary: Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia has plunged the AI industry into uncharted territory — a corporate earthquake that dwarfs even the chaos unleashed by Sam Altman's temporary firing from OpenAI in 2023. Why it matters: Nvidia is the backbone of the global AI economy , with its chips, investments and financial guarantees sustaining an entire ecosystem of companies worth trillions of dollars. At the center of that vast financial flywheel is Huang, who spent 33 years making himself synonymous with Nvidia — and Nvidia synonymous with the AI revolution. "This is no ordinary CEO. This is no ordinary company. This is no ordinary sector. This is no ordinary time," economist Mohamed El-Erian wrote on X , warning of contagion across the AI industry. The latest: Huang resigned from all his positions at Nvidia, the company's board of directors said Thursday, following allegations of two affairs, including one with a woman accused of being a spy for China. The board named Nvidia's CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO. Zoom in: As recently as two weeks ago, the notion of Nvidia without Jensen was unthinkable. Even after his affair with Alice Huang — the woman suspected of being a Chinese spy — came to light, President Trump and Nvidia's board stood behind him, Silicon Valley's elite rallied to his defense and betting markets suggested he would survive. It took revelations of a second affair — this time with an executive who reported directly to Jensen Huang — to shatter that consensus and bring his storied reign to the brink of a stunning end. Driving the news: After that second affair came to light Wednesday night, Nvidia's board reportedly met to settle Huang's fate. The White House was read in. The market reaction has been brutal. Nvidia had already shed more than $1 trillion in market value since the initial scandal erupted, and shares plunged further in after-hours and pre-market trading overnight. One of Wall Street's most prominent voices on tech, analyst Dan Ives, said Nvidia was worth 25% less without Huang. Zoom out: Huang's rise was the stuff of Silicon Valley legend: The Taiwanese immigrant went from cleaning toilets at a Kentucky boarding school and waiting tables at Denny's to building one of the most valuable companies in history. Huang and two fellow engineers hatched the idea for Nvidia at a Denny's booth in 1993, launching a chipmaker that would revolutionize gaming, transform modern computing and ultimately power the AI revolution. Clad in his trademark black leather jacket, Huang became a global AI rock star — with a cult of personality that drew adoring crowds, calmed markets and commanded the attention of world leaders. The big picture: Huang's apparent downfall comes amid mounting anxiety over the AI industry's future, as new financial, political and regulatory risks threaten one of the largest infrastructure buildouts in history. The timing is especially fraught for Anthropic , whose historic IPO — backed by a $10 billion commitment from Nvidia — looms as a referendum on Wall Street's faith in the AI trade. Huang spent years defending the industry's soaring valuations and dismissing warnings of a speculative frenzy. Now his own scandals could help burst the bubble he insisted didn't exist. What to watch: The blast radius could extend far beyond Silicon Valley and Wall Street, threatening to engulf the Trump administration in a scandal over its handling of sensitive technology exports to China. Huang forged a close alliance with Trump and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick , who loosened restrictions on chip sales even as other officials raised concerns about Chinese espionage and smuggling. Top Senate Democrats are already demanding that Lutnick and other senior officials preserve records of their dealings with Nvidia and Huang, laying the groundwork for a sweeping investigation. The bottom line: As veteran China watcher Bill Bishop wrote after Huang acknowledged his first affair: "There is rarely just one lie." Editor's note: This story has been updated with news of Jensen Huang's resignation from Nvidia.

events.title: A New Dawn in the Cloud: ‘Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War IV’ Is Coming to GeForce NOW
events.summary: Rally the ranks this GFN Thursday. Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War IV is coming to GeForce NOW , allowing players to experience the battle for Kronus through cloud gaming. There’s more on the horizon, with NVIDIA DLSS 5 technology coming to War Thunder and Where Winds Meet . Meanwhile, Dragon’s Dogma 2: Dark Arisen brings new tales and encounters, alongside 10 games joining the GeForce NOW library this week. Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War IV , developed by KING Art Games and published by Deep Silver, is coming to GeForce NOW. Launching on Steam Thursday, Dec. 3, the real-time strategy game returns to the series’ roots with large-scale battles, base building and a renewed fight for planet Kronus. Command the Space Marines, Orks, Necrons or the Adeptus Mechanicus, which makes their series debut. Build a base, secure resources and customize squads to the conflict across more than 70 campaign missions, playable solo or in co-op mode. The Last Stand, Skirmish and multiplayer modes offer more ways to put tactics to the test. GeForce NOW will bring the action to supported PCs, Macs, handhelds and other devices, with game downloads and updates handled in the cloud. Save the storage space for everyday essentials and planning for the next offensive. Wishlist the game on Steam , and stay tuned to GFN Thursday to prepare for launch. NVIDIA DLSS 5 continues to evolve, with Gaijin Entertainment’s War Thunder and Everstone Studio’s Where Winds Meet next to receive support for the technology with the 3D-Guided Neural Rendering feature. Arriving in mid-November, War Thunder ’s Eagle’s Shadow major update adds DLSS 5 with 3D-Guided Neural Rendering, dozens of new planes, ships and tanks, along with cluster bombs for planes and visual-effects enhancements increasing the realism and dynamism of battle. In Where Winds Meet , DLSS support arrives Monday, Nov. 23, enhancing the environments and characters of its wuxia open-world action role-playing game. Both titles will use the latest DLSS 5 with 3D-Guided Neural Rendering model, released in October, which doubles model performance compared with the previous version. Since its initial announcement in March, model performance has improved tenfold, bringing the technology to more gamers, including GeForce NOW Ultimate members streaming with GeForce RTX 5080 cloud rigs. Get a closer look at the DLSS updates and find more details . Dragon’s Dogma 2: Dark Arisen is streaming on GeForce NOW, expanding the deep, explorable fantasy world of Dragon’s Dogma 2 with new tales and encounters. Travel to the long-abandoned region of Norgan, join the enigmatic Eir and uncover the secrets of the undying Fallen Dragon. Unearth forgotten relics to unlock powerful weapons and skills, take on Lost Rites’ 12 dungeon challenges and explore new hairstyles and tattoos for Arisen and Pawn customization. Delicious in Dungeon also arrives in the world of Dragon’s Dogma 2: Dark Arisen with a special collaboration. GeForce NOW keeps all the new downloadable content available across supported devices — without a single download claiming local storage on a gamer’s hardware of choice. In addition, members can look for the following games joining the GeForce NOW library this week: Worst Class Ever (New release on Steam , Nov. 9) Ashes of the Singularity II (New release on Steam , Nov. 10) Cyberpunk 2077 ( Xbox Play Anywhere, new release on Battle.net , Nov. 10) DreamWorks Shrek 2 Remastered (New release on Steam , Nov. 10) Warhammer Survivors (New release on Steam and Xbox , available on Game Pass, Nov. 10) Main Sequence (New release on Steam , Nov. 12) GeForce 8800 GTX – 20 Years of a Legend ( Steam , Ultimate members) Also this week, Ultimate members can take a trip back to 2006 with GeForce 8800 GTX – 20 Years of a Legend , a playable demo celebrating the iconic GPU’s 20th anniversary with DLSS 4.5 and path tracing in the cloud. Dates listed above reflect when games are released on their respective stores. GeForce NOW availability may vary, as games are onboarded after release and added throughout the week. Keep an eye on GeForce NOW channels and GFN Thursdays for availability updates on announced titles. events.title: A new AI model wants to read between the lines
events.summary: The Scoop New York-based AI startup millionways on Thursday launched its new AI model that claims to offer insight into human intent and motivations. The company also told Semafor it has raised $6 million in US funding, with investors including football stars Jason Kelce and DK Metcalf. The Thorsten-4 model was born out of a research project in Germany in which dozens of psychologists interviewed more than 7,000 people about their personal lives and aspirations. That data — which the psychologists labeled by hand to capture what people’s words revealed about their motives and thinking — was used to train the model. Millionways cofounders Martin Cordsmeier and Max Weidemann argue that understanding is missing from regular AI models, which are trained on internet text. They see the model as particularly useful in sales and executive hiring, where a search firm could prompt it to evaluate an interview transcript to gauge how a candidate will behave under pressure. “We can add a level of human understanding that the language models cannot get to by themselves,” Weidemann said, adding that the model should be “a decision-making support tool rather than the ultimate decision-maker.” J.D.’s view Enterprises are increasingly injecting task- and industry-specific models into their tech stacks, rather than defaulting to the frontier models for every task. Just this week, leading voice AI company ElevenLabs, for example, announced a healthcare-focused version of its new transcription model. This gives CIOs more choice and customization, but it also adds the burden of testing whether specialized models actually beat fast-improving frontier ones. Cordsmeier and Weidemann ran our conversation for this story through Thorsten-4, which deduced that I was most focused on relationship-building and being conscientious: “You move between logic and intuition, and tough questions energized you.” (I’ll take the compliment!) I ran a transcript of the same call through Anthropic’s new Claude Fable 5.2 model and asked for a psychology analysis: Claude also gave a solid assessment, though it was less sure of itself, focusing more on the job I was doing than on me as a person. It (correctly) noted that my “unstated goal was source cultivation.”

events.summary: U.S. Energy Information Administration - EIA - Independent Statistics and Analysis Browse by tag liquid fuels natural gas electricity oil/petroleum production/supply crude oil consumption/demand generation prices map states exports/imports international coal renewables weather forecasts/projections gasoline capacity steo (short-term energy outlook) Data source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Short-Term Energy Outlook , November 2026 After decades of decline , crude oil production in Alaska is growing, driven by two projects on Alaska’s North Slope. In our latest Short-Term Energy Outlook , we expect a 23,000 barrels per day (b/d) (6%) increase in 2026, followed by a 60,000 b/d (13%) rise in 2027. At a forecast 505,000 b/d in 2027, output would be the most since 2014. If realized, these annual production increases will be the largest since the 1980s, when Alaskan crude production peaked at 2.0 million b/d. The recent growth is attributable to two projects on Alaska's North Slope: The Nuna project, owned by ConocoPhillips, started production in December 2024 and is expected to produce 20,000 b/d at its peak. So far this year, it has produced an average of 10,000 b/d, partially offsetting existing production declines. The Pikka Phase 1 project, jointly owned by Santos and Repsol, began production in May 2026 with initial average monthly production of 2,000 b/d and reaching 38,000 b/d as of September 2026, according to data from the Alaska Oil & Gas Conservation Commission . We expect peak production of 80,000 b/d by winter 2026–27, nearly 20% of total Alaskan production in 2025. Notably, our STEO production data indicate that third-quarter 2026 production grew 4% as Pikka Phase 1 came online, marking the first third-quarter production increase in more than 40 years. Alaskan crude output typically dips in late summer when operators conduct annual maintenance, running an average of 7% lower than first-quarter levels over the previous five years (2021–2025). events.title: Jensen Huang Resigns as Nvidia CEO
events.summary: Jensen Huang stepped down as the chief executive of Nvidia on Thursday, four days after the company announced its internal investigation into an affair he had with Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, an alleged asset of China’s Ministry of State Security. “Jensen Huang has resigned as President, Chief Executive Officer, and a member of the Board, effective immediately,” the Nvidia board said in a statement. Nvidia’s chief financial officer, Colette Kress, will serve as interim CEO. The board said it “will consider internal and external candidates” for a permanent replacement. The board’s investigation was announced on November 8, slightly less than two weeks after The New York Times reported that the chief executive had been the target of a Chinese intelligence operation facilitated through his relationship with Alice Huang, who has no known relation to Jensen. The pair have been spotted in public together at least twice, in June 2024 and May 2025 . On November 11, The New York Times reported that Jensen Huang also allegedly had a relationship with a direct report at Nvidia. The alleged relationship with a subordinate, along with Huang’s business dealings with Megaspeed, a Singapore-based AI company where Alice Huang previously held a senior position, likely played a greater role in the board’s decision to oust Huang than the Chinese espionage allegations, a source familiar with the matter tells WIRED. US intelligence officials reportedly briefed President Donald Trump on Huang’s relationship with Alice last year, but the president did not act on it. On November 6, The New York Times and Financial Times reported that Alice was a spy for China’s Ministry of State Security and that she had been recruited to collect information on the Nvidia executive. (The Chinese government has rejected all claims that Alice was a spy for the country. ) Huang sent a companywide email on Sunday acknowledging his affair, apologizing to his family and Nvidia employees, and pledging cooperation with the internal investigation. The executive has been married to his wife, Lori Huang, since 1985 , and both of the couple’s two children work at the company. On Monday, WIRED exclusively reported that last year Huang began working with a crisis PR firm to manage his personal communications. In October 2025, those PR consultants started to be looped in on all press inquiries involving Huang, whether those inquiries were personal or professional in nature. The timing lines up with a New York Times report that month that the US Commerce Department was investigating whether Alice Huang’s Megaspeed was helping Chinese companies get around American export controls with the help of a vast web of subsidiaries. The investigation was reportedly halted and transferred to the Justice Department after Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter inquired about it. Huang has been a vocal critic of these export controls, which he argues unnecessarily constrain the market for American chips, create discrete Chinese and American tech ecosystems, and spur China to build competitive chips of its own. Huang has worked to develop a relationship with Trump in order to advocate for policies that are advantageous for Nvidia, including the idea of opening its markets to China. Huang cofounded Nvidia in 1993 with friends Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem. The trio reportedly brainstormed their vision for the company in a Denny’s diner and aspired to bring realistic 3D graphics to personal computers. For the first few decades of its existence, Nvidia was primarily known in the gaming community for creating chips powerful enough to render high-quality in-game graphics. In 2012, after a new kind of neural network known as AlexNet won a high-profile prize in computer vision, Nvidia pivoted from high-speed computer graphics to building chips that would support artificial intelligence. Huang has repeatedly said that the introduction of AlexNet, which was developed by AI engineers Alex Krizhevsky, Ilya Sutskever, and Geoffrey Hinton, was a “Big Bang”–like event for computing. Because its new GPUs proved highly effective at powering AI models that require massive amounts of processing power, the value of Nvidia shares soared in 2023 and 2024, in lockstep with the broader AI boom that began sweeping through the world economy. In the summer of 2025, Nvidia became the first company in history to cross $4 trillion in value. As of September 2026, the company controlled about 90 percent of the GPU market. Much of Nvidia’s epic rise over the few decades has been attributed not just to its cutting-edge chips and its software “moat,” CUDA, that keeps developers locked into those chips, but also to the fast-thinking, controlling, charismatic, and often bombastic leadership style of Huang himself. Now, that critical part of the company’s success is out.

events.title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO after affair with suspected Chinese spy
events.summary: Embattled Nvidia co-founder and chief executive Jensen Huang has resigned, marking a stunning fall from grace for the leader of a vital US computing giant that has long helped to fuel the artificial intelligence boom. Mr Huang’s departure came days after he admitted to having an affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. In a statement, Nvidia's board of directors thanked Mr Jensen for his "profound" contributions to the company. "The board and the company thank Jensen for his immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry," the statement read. Colette Kress, current executive vice president and chief financial officer, will serve as interim chief executive, Nvidia announced. Nvidia stock was closed down 4.44 per cent, much steeper than the Nasdaq's drop of 0.39 per cent. Harvey Jones, chairman of Nvidia's board of directors, said Ms Kress had helped lead the company through a “period of extraordinary growth and has a deep understanding of our business, customers, operations and financial position”. “She is supported by an experienced leadership team that has been instrumental in executing Nvidia's strategy and advancing its technology road map." Political fallout US President Donald Trump , a long-time ally of Mr Huang, posted about the AI tycoon's departure on Truth Social, the US President's social media platform. "Now that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one man to take his place: Tim Cook of Apple," Mr Trump wrote. "A legend replaces a legend." Mr Huang's many meetings with Mr Trump, however, often brought controversy. He would lobby Mr Trump to try to relax US chip export policies affecting China, which caused an uproar with both Democrats and Republicans. Jensen Huang’s decision to resign from NVIDIA does not absolve him, other executives, or the company as a whole of responsibility for putting our national security at risk or for any potential violations of our laws. They still owe Congress answers. — Elizabeth Warren (@SenWarren) November 12, 2026 Democratic senator Elizabeth Warren on Thursday claimed Mr Trump and those he appointed to the Department of Commerce enabled some of the controversies that engulfed Nvidia. " Secretary Howard Lutnick and undersecretary Jeffrey Kessler must explain why they have not closed export control loopholes and act today to ensure our advanced technology is not fuelling China’s military," she said, referring to reports of Nvidia's dealings with China. Alice Huang affair Mr Huang, who co-founded Nvidia in 1993, sparked a crisis this month when he admitted to having an affair with Alice Huang, a technology executive. US officials and investigators said they believe Ms Huang, who is not related to Mr Huang, to be a spy working on behalf of China, the top US rival in the tech and AI field. To maintain its edge in the AI race, the US introduced export policies designed to keep some of the most powerful US-made semiconductors and computers away from adversaries. But Mr Huang and Nvidia openly opposed the export policies. He said the restrictions hampered US influence and prevented American technology from becoming a global standard. Proponents of the export policies, however, said they strengthened the US lead and made it difficult for countries such as China to catch up, particularly in the need for computing power to train large language models. Some of those supporters of the export policies accused Nvidia and Mr Huang of wanting to boost revenue at all costs, even if detrimental to US national security. As the overall mood towards AI, Big Tech executives and unregulated technology began to sour among US voters, politicians increased scrutiny of Nvidia. Infidelity By the time Mr Huang admitted to the affair, media reports had accused his company of ignoring various products entering China. Mr Huang’s admission of infidelity expedited and amplified calls for further inquiries. Shortly after his confession, Nvidia’s board of directors announced an independent investigation to address reports of whether he had been the target of a foreign spy operation and what, if anything, had been compromised. Company representatives initially insisted Mr Huang would remain chief executive but pressure grew. He founded Nvidia, with Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem, in 1993, as the personal computer sector was booming. A major part of that was gaming but many computers were not designed for gamers and Nvidia saw an opening in the market. The company designed special graphics cards and video boards that, while popular, did not make Nvidia a household name. As a result, its name was mispronounced by many for a long time. Profits steadily grew, however, and the company methodically expanded. As progress in AI started to hit its stride, Nvidia soon found its custom graphics processing units and boards in unprecedented demand. Stuff of legend Nvidia could hardly build its products fast enough to keep up with demand, yet it knew how to make them to perfection. Revenue and profits soared, and Mr Huang’s presence became almost impossible to ignore, even among those who had no interest in AI. His work ethic and management style became famous. At one point, CBS did an interview inside a Denny’s restaurant where he had spent many late nights founding the company. It was the sort of story that exemplified the American dream, But as Nvidia and Mr Huang enjoyed unprecedented success, some US officials raised concerns that Nvidia’s profits were being generated at the expense of national security, with its products potentially being used by hackers and hostile governments. Mr Huang’s fuelled more questions about Nvidia’s governance. His exit probably eclipses Apple’s dismissal of Steve Jobs in 1985, which was mainly caused by a boardroom power struggle. Who is interim chief executive Colette Kress? Within a few hours of being named Nvidia's chief executive, Ms Kress told the company’s more than 42,000 employees that she believes in Nvidia's future. "I recognise that this has been an extraordinarily difficult period and I want you to know how grateful we are for your resilience, professionalism and continued dedication," she wrote. Ms Kress said a company-wide meeting would take place on November 18, where more announcements would be made. "We play a vital role in building the technology that is powering the Al revolution, and we have important work ahead of us," she wrote. Ms Kress was previously chief financial officer for US technology company Cisco, and before that was a corporate vice president of Microsoft, from 2006 to 2010. According to her LinkedIn profile, Ms Kress earned a master's from from the Southern Methodist University's Cox School of Business in Dallas, Texas. For undergraduate studies, she attended the University of Arizona.

events.title: Trump orders Vance to focus on "corruption" in Democrat-run areas, not Iran
events.summary: President Trump directed Vice President JD Vance on Thursday to turn his "complete and total attention" toward alleged corruption in Democrat-run cities and states, contending that "[w]e don't need a deal with Iran." The big picture: After Vance concluded that the Iran war drove Republicans' stunning midterm walloping, Trump is reorienting his No. 2's focus — and directing him to go after Democrats the president labeled as "CORRUPT AND EVIL." Oil prices surged, and stocks sank after Trump's post reinjected a note of uncertainty into a market that was acting like the Iran war was all but over. Driving the news: "We don't need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed," Trump wrote on Truth Social. Also on Truth Social Thursday, he threatened new tariffs on Mexico and criticized GOP senators for failing to pass the Save America ACT — adding that failure to do so was "devastating" for Republicans during the midterms. He said that he had asked Vance to "focus his complete and total attention" on so-called "Corruption and Crime" in Democrat-run cities and states, naming Minnesota, California and Illinois. Vance has chaired Trump's Task Force to Eliminate Fraud since the president created it via executive order earlier this year. Throughout the first half of his administration and federal crackdown on U.S. cities, Trump has repeatedly framed blue areas as hotbeds of crime and corruption, even when the stats haven't necessarily backed up those arguments. Catch up quick: Vance was recently heavily involved in a push to reach a new ceasefire with Iran and resume nuclear negotiations, Axios' Barak Ravid reported. Vance was a skeptical voice in Trump's inner circle about the war, Ravid reported, and led U.S. negotiating delegations after it began. Vance's office and the White House did not immediately respond to Axios' request for comment. Between the lines: Vance offered a surprisingly candid assessment of the midterm shellacking, writing in an X post last week that "[t]he reason we lost is the war." He continued: "If you'd like to argue it was worth it, that losing the Senate for the next 6 years was worth it, then do so. Argue it was a worthwhile cost to pay. Agree or disagree, that's at least honest." "But everyone knows why we lost." What we're watching: Secretary of State Marco Rubio met with his G7 counterparts in Paris on Tuesday, where he said Trump had considered resuming the war or cutting a deal but instead settled on strangling the Iranian regime, Axios previously reported . Rubio has signaled skepticism of a diplomatic breakthrough — and Trump's post indicates that door is closed, for now. Editor's note: The story has been updated with additional information. events.title: NVIDIA Announces CEO Transition
events.summary: Colette Kress, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, Appointed Interim CEO Harvey C. Jones Appointed First-Ever Chair of the Board NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) Board of Directors announced today that Jensen Huang has resigned as President, Chief Executive Officer, and a member of the Board, effective immediately. Colette Kress, current Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of NVIDIA, has agreed to serve as Interim Chief Executive Officer. Kress will continue to serve as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer while serving as Interim Chief Executive Officer until a permanent successor has been named. The Board is initiating a search for a permanent Chief Executive Officer and will consider internal and external candidates. Kress has served as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of NVIDIA since joining the company in September 2013. During her tenure, she has led the company’s finance organization and has played a key role in NVIDIA’s growth and evolution. Prior to joining NVIDIA, Kress spent nearly 25 years in finance roles at leading technology companies, including Cisco and Microsoft. The Board of Directors appointed Harvey C. Jones as its first-ever Chair of the Board. Mr. Jones has been an entrepreneur, technology executive, and active venture investor for over 30 years, including serving as Chief Executive Officer and Executive Chairman of Synopsys. “Colette has helped lead NVIDIA through a period of extraordinary growth and has a deep understanding of our business, customers, operations and financial position,” said Harvey Jones, Chair of the NVIDIA Board of Directors. “She is supported by an experienced leadership team that has been instrumental in executing NVIDIA’s strategy and advancing its technology roadmap. The Board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team, and we expect the company’s operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption.” “NVIDIA’s strength has always come from its people, and together with our leadership team, I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years,” said Colette Kress, Interim CEO and CFO, NVIDIA. “We will continue advancing the work that has made NVIDIA a leader in accelerated computing and AI, and execute on the opportunities ahead. Our focus remains on serving our customers, partners, developers and shareholders.” Jensen’s contributions to NVIDIA are profound. NVIDIA is one of the most consequential technology companies in the world. The Board and the company thank Jensen for his immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry. NVIDIA will report its third-quarter fiscal 2027 financial results on Tuesday, November 17, at approximately 1:20 p.m. PT, as previously scheduled, followed by its earnings call at 2 p.m. PT.
